title: Research (no κ claim): Gaussian E8 c = 20 exact certificates; local-rewrite census on #4088's T360 words
body:
**No κ claim.** This continues #620's Gaussian-E8 notes (§13–§16, merged) and adds one negative census on the current T360 frontier words.

## 1. Gaussian E8, c = 20 — exact certificates (`research/e8-gaussian-c20-exact/`)
A Gaussian-E8 decoder (60 ℚ(i)-lines, F2 pattern) beats real E8 only if its Theorem-C cost is ≤ 42. §15–§16 exclude c ≤ 19.

| cost cap | cases | status |
|---|---|---|
| ≤ 41 | 20 | **all excluded** |
| ≤ 42 | 21 | **16 excluded**; open: 5, 6, 17, 18, 23 |

- **So no 20-total Gaussian decoder costs ≤ 41.**
- At cost 42, the five open cases sit within 1 of the counting threshold. They may be counting-feasible, in which case only the F2 pattern (e.g. §16's 2×2 support lemma) can close them.
- **Method:** an exact branch-and-bound (`ebb4.py`). HiGHS solves the LPs, every bound is recomputed from dyadic-rounded duals in integer arithmetic, probing and reduced-cost fixing are recorded as certified steps, and symmetry is reduced with each case's stabilizer.
- **Checking:** each certificate is re-checked **without floating point** by `ecert.py`.
- **Reproduce:** `sh verify.sh /fresh/dir` rebuilds every table from scratch and reports `verified 35 / 35 certificates EXCLUDED (exact)`, as tested locally from a clean directory.
- **Case 22's certificate (349 MB)** exceeds GitHub's limit. Its SHA-256, our exact check and the deterministic regeneration command are included.

## 2. Local-rewrite census on #4088's T360 words (`research/t360-local-rewrite-census/`)
Searched on the #4088 head (`72d7efc1`), with a full frame re-solve after every candidate:
- receiver sharing (#4085's identity, dyadic ratios, clusters of up to 8);
- source sharing;
- commuting-gate retiming.

About 20,000 candidates across the A, B and restore stages gave **0 strict savings**, and the current frames are already optimal. The only payable receiver pair, 672/676 via 544, is the one #4085 already uses. Further 8→7 staged entries are capped by owner sink capacity (#4076's LP, #4091's ceiling).

**Credits:**
- Gaussian line: #595, #446, #620, #738, #767, #770, #801, #868, #888, #2066.
- T360 census: #4088 (1337isnot1337), #4085 (zxv; Nick Petalas's fan-out search), #4076 and #3945 (rohanarun), #3949, #4091 (RossRichardson).
